transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Product Security) — Liam O'Connor (CISO, Guardian Health), Priya Singh (Head of Security), Ava Morales (Eng Manager), Tom Evans (DevOps)
Shared artifacts: redwood/pen-test-results-2026-02.pdf (link), mitigation-spreadsheet.xlsx (shared drive), SOC2-controls-mapping-v2.docx (link)

Summary:
Quick review of most recent pen test findings, discussion of vulnerability management and secure SDLC practices, specifics on patching cadence and how Redwood surfaces critical CVEs in Dedicated/Private deployments, clarifying RBAC/SSO and KMS/encryption posture. Agreed next steps include Redwood sending redacted pen-test PDF + mitigation spreadsheet and scheduling a follow-up to align on SOC2 scope and patch cadence.

Topics:
- High/Medium/Low findings from pen test (auth, insecure config, info leak)
- Vulnerability triage and prioritization workflow
- Patch cadence and emergency patching / SLOs
- Secure SDLC: PR gating, SCA, dependency scanning
- Encryption and KMS key management for Private deployments
- Audit logs, retention, and access controls (RBAC/SAML/SCIM)
- Data residency and regional isolation for PHI

Action items (captured above): see action_items field.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: ok hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we'll do a quick run through the pen test results we shared earlier, and then go into vuln mgmt and patching cadence, please call out any questions.
00:14 Liam O'Connor: thanks Maya, and uh just to frame, Guardian Health is under an RFP for SOC2 and some NHS integrations later this year so we need to make sure the pen test items map to our control set, and we need timelines on mitigations.
00:28 Diego Ruiz: understood, we'll try to map findings back to SOC2 and ISO where possible. quick note, the PDF we uploaded is redacted for 3rd party IP and internal hostnames.
00:45 Priya Singh: right, first question — there's an authentication bypass listed as a high finding, can you summarize the root cause and whether it's exploitable in hosted vs private?
01:02 Samir Patel: sure, that one was related to a legacy oauth redirect handling on a decommissioned endpoint; exploitability was moderate because it required an unprivileged account and knowledge of a deprecated param. in Hosted it's mitigated by our gateway WAF rules and runtime routing; in Dedicated/Private customers who pin older model endpoints could be exposed if they haven't applied our recent runtime patch.
01:30 Tom Evans: when you say runtime patch are those pushed automatically for Hosted and Dedicated? how about Private on-prem?
01:40 Diego Ruiz: Hosted - yes auto-deploys with our standard maintenance window. Dedicated - we push to clusters but customers can opt for a maintenance window; we strongly recommend the immediate patch. Private (on-prem/VPC) - we provide the patch bundle and instructions; automatic apply depends on customer's operational policy.
02:02 Ava Morales: ok so for Private we would be responsible to apply? that changes our timelines. what support do you offer for emergency patches?
02:12 Maya Chen: we have an emergency patch runbook and can provide a managed patch assistance add-on for Private customers; Diego can follow up with steps.
02:21 Diego Ruiz: yeah i'll attach the runbook, and we can offer a short engagement where our ops team helps apply the patch in a weekend window.
02:33 Liam O'Connor: noted. another medium finding mentions info disclosure via logs, says 'sensitive tokens in debug logs' — is that in customer logs or internal?
02:48 Samir Patel: that was mostly around verbose debug in a staging path where trace IDs and partial tokens were logged. impacted customers are those who enabled verbose logging. we now mask tokens at the logging layer, and our log retention default is 30 days but we can adjust to customer needs.
03:07 Priya Singh: and retention/exports — we need audit logs that align with our SOC2 requirements, with immutable export for 90 days at least. can you do that?
03:18 Diego Ruiz: we support audit logs via the Console with export to S3 or customer controlled bucket; retention can be configured and we can set WORM for exports if the customer wants immutable storage.
03:30 Tom Evans: any limits on log volume or queries for long term retention? we expect fairly high volume due to telemetry.
03:41 Diego Ruiz: there's tiered log retention add-ons, and for Dedicated we can increase ingestion rates. for Private you manage the bucket so limits are what your infra supports, but Redwood's export tooling streams to any configured endpoint.
03:56 Liam O'Connor: on encryption and KMS, we need BYOK and HSM-backed keys for PHI. can you confirm capabilities across Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
04:10 Samir Patel: Hosted - we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and GCP KMS integrations, but HSM-backed via CloudHSM is supported through a contract path; Dedicated - we can bring KMS integration at cluster level, and for Private we fully support on-prem HSM/KMS; keys never leave customer control in BYOK modes.
04:36 Ava Morales: how is key rotation handled and audited?
04:40 Diego Ruiz: rotation is configurable, we emit key rotation events to audit logs, and we can provide rotation scripts or link to your KMS for automatic rotation.
04:52 Priya Singh: good. on RBAC and SSO we need SCIM provisioning and SAML2.0; there was a note about inconsistent role mappings in the report. can you expand?
05:06 Maya Chen: yes the pen test flagged a misconfiguration in a legacy role sync job that could map a restricted role to a broader permission set during a sync failure. we've fixed the sync job and added unit tests + a canary to prevent regressions.
05:23 Liam O'Connor: do you support fine-grained roles for audit-only vs admin? we need separation of duties.
05:29 Diego Ruiz: yes we have a role model with admin, operator, auditor, and custom role support. auditing-only roles can be restricted to read-only views and export-only privileges.
05:40 Ava Morales: will the fix be included in the SOC2 evidence pack?
05:45 Samir Patel: yes, we'll include the remediation evidence and change-failure blameless notes. Maya will link the SOC2 mapping doc.
05:54 Liam O'Connor: moving to vuln mgmt — how do you triage CVEs that affect the runtime and model artifacts? what's your SLA on critical CVEs?
06:06 Diego Ruiz: we classify based on exploitability and impact. critical CVEs get a 72-hour mitigation plan with either workaround, hotfix, or mitigation and a timeline to full patch. for Hosted we typically patch within the 72 hour window; for Dedicated we coordinate maintenance windows; for Private we provide hotfixes and runbook.
06:28 Priya Singh: do you publish a CVE dashboard and do customers get notification via email and Console?
06:34 Diego Ruiz: yes notifications go via console, email integration, and webhooks for ticketing systems. we also have an RSS/atom feed for CVE advisories.
06:44 Tom Evans: what about dependency scanning and SCA in CI for your open-source components?
06:49 Samir Patel: we run SBOM generation and SCA scans on our releases. results feed into our vulnerability tracker and are triaged by Product Security. we also run pre-release static analysis and some fuzz tests for critical components.
07:05 Ava Morales: do you share SBOMs with customers?
07:08 Diego Ruiz: yes we provide SBOMs under NDA or in our customer portal for deployed versions.
07:13 Liam O'Connor: the pen test calls out a cross-tenant data exposure scenario, medium risk, can you walk us through mitigations?
07:24 Samir Patel: that one was due to an edge-case in a multi-tenant cache routing rule. mitigation was to add tenant context checks and tighten KV cache scoping; we also added regression tests and a monitoring alert for unusual cross-tenant access patterns.
07:42 Priya Singh: is that mitigated in the patch you mentioned earlier?
07:45 Diego Ruiz: yes it's included.
07:47 Maya Chen: quick commercial note, for Dedicated we can schedule a forced patching window if you want us to coordinate and apply the fixes.
07:57 Tom Evans: on patch cadence — what's your regular cadence and emergency process? we run quarterly for infra, monthly for apps, but for security we do weekly scans.
08:10 Diego Ruiz: standard cadence: minor runtime updates monthly, major releases quarterly. security-critical patches are treated as exceptions and can be pushed in the emergency window; we recommend customers subscribe to our security channel.
08:24 Ava Morales: and does Redwood sign an SLA for time-to-patch for critical security issues?
08:29 Maya Chen: SLA depends on plan. Enterprise Dedicated has contractual response windows; we can add specific patch SLAs into a contract.
08:36 Liam O'Connor: ok that helps. next — secure SDLC: can you summarize your CI gates and how you prevent vulnerable deps from being released?
08:48 Samir Patel: we block merges if SCA finds high severity unpatched dependencies; we have automated test gating, PR linting, static analysis alerts, and mandatory code owner reviews for critical paths. we also run canary deploys and automated rollback on errors.
09:06 Priya Singh: do you use SNYK or similar? what's your tooling?
09:10 Diego Ruiz: we use a mix — SCA via a commercial scanner plus in-house heuristics. we also run a periodic dependency sweep for transitive deps.
09:20 Ava Morales: for evidence, can you provide pipeline screenshots and policies?
09:24 Maya Chen: yes we'll include screenshots and a short video of the gated pipeline in the evidence bundle.
09:31 Liam O'Connor: data residency question — we have PHI and need EU residency for some cohorts; can you guarantee model compute and logs stay in region?
09:41 Diego Ruiz: yes we support region pinning for compute and separate log buckets; for Hosted we have European regions and we can pin compute + storage. for Dedicated we can deploy to your preferred region; for Private you control the region entirely.
09:54 Priya Singh: what about backups and replication across regions — any default cross-region copies?
10:00 Samir Patel: default Hosted backups may replicate for resilience; we can disable cross-region replication for sensitive customers and provide single-region retention.
10:10 Liam O'Connor: good. any outstanding medium findings we should prioritize?
10:16 Maya Chen: we highlighted token-in-logs, role-sync misconfig, multi-tenant cache rule, and a misconfigured CSP header on a static asset. we recommend priorities: 1) auth bug (high) 2) cache scoping (medium-high) 3) token logging (medium) 4) CSP / static assets (low-medium).
10:34 Priya Singh: acceptable. can you provide estimated remediation timelines per item?
10:38 Diego Ruiz: auth bug - patched now, rollout tonight for Hosted, Dedicated within 48 hours; Private will get a hotfix bundle within 72 hours. cache scoping - patch in QA, targeted rollouts next week; token logging - immediate config change done, will confirm in spreadsheet; CSP - config update in next release.
10:56 Liam O'Connor: great. on evidence for audits — we need change logs, PRs, and test results. do you include those?
11:05 Samir Patel: yes we can provide redacted PRs, test artifacts, and CI logs, plus the remediation verification steps.
11:12 Ava Morales: one last operational question — how do you handle emergency rollback if a patch causes regressions?
11:18 Diego Ruiz: automatic rollback policies on canary failures, and for Dedicated we maintain nightly backups and rollback images; Private customers we provide rollback images and runbooks.
11:30 Maya Chen: ok time check — about 10 minutes left, let's recap next steps.
11:35 Liam O'Connor: please send the redacted pen test and mitigation sheet and we'll review internally with SOC2 team. also would like to see the SBOM for the runtime.
11:46 Maya Chen: noted — Diego will send the spreadsheet and Samir will attach the SBOM and SOC2 mapping doc. we'll set the follow up for 2026-03-08 to discuss patch cadence and contract SLAs.
11:58 Priya Singh: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
12:02 Tom Evans: thanks, i'll pull our patch cadence doc and share before the follow up.
12:08 Diego Ruiz: i'll send the runbook and evidence links by 2026-02-25.
12:12 Maya Chen: thanks all, bye.

End transcript.
